abstract.para: The toolchain components include the following tools: the GNU C library, the GCC and G++ compilers, binutils, GDB and LLVM. Each component has its own update strategy, described in the corresponding sections.

listitem.para: Stable
The initial version is 2.40. The package is updated with each minor release if there are reasons for changes, for example feature requests or performance tuning.
Updates are backward compatible for dynamic linking, so programs built on earlier &suselinux; 16 releases keep running.
Symbols deprecated in upstream glibc are not declared for the compiler and are not available for link editing (static linking).

section.title: Compiler for user space applications and libraries
section.para: Developers of user-space applications can use the supported GNU Compiler Collection (GCC) C and C++ built-in compilers. Compilers for other languages, cross-compilers and accelerator offloading compilers are not available on &suselinux; from standard repositories. Developers can install them from PackageHub with community support.

listitem.para: Agile, with the tick-tock model described below.
GCC 15 in &suselinux; 16.1. The tick-tock model applies to later releases.

Introduce a new major GCC version as the default compiler. It is supported during LTS of the introducing minor release and of the next minor release. Example: GCC 17, introduced in 16.2, is supported until the end of LTS of 16.3.

Include a new non-default major GCC version. To use it, invoke the binaries gcc-x, g++-x and gfortran-x explicitly. Non-default versions are supported for 24 months. In 16.1, this is GCC 16, invoked with gcc-16, g++-16 and gfortran-16.

section.title: Supported compiler flags
section.para: Any combination of the following compiler flags is supported:

listitem.para: -O0, -O2 and -O3
-fpie and -fno-pie

section.para: The following options are also supported on &x86-64;:

listitem.para: -march=x86-64-v2 (the default one)

section.para: Other compiler flags are not supported by &suse;. &suse; can assist in reporting issues to the upstream GCC project.

listitem.para: ISO/IEC 9899:2024 (C23) with GNU extensions
With the default GCC 15: ISO/IEC 14882:2017 (C++17) with GNU extensions. With the non-default GCC 16: ISO/IEC 14882:2020 (C++20) with GNU extensions.
Up to Fortran 95 (ISO/IEC 1539:1997), with specific features from later standards as described in the manual.
Building a kernel module requires the same compiler version that was used to build the kernel. &suse; therefore provides that GCC version, initially GCC 13.N.
The compiler is not intended for general use and may be dropped in a future minor release.
&suselinux; 16 packages are built internally with GCC 13. This build compiler is provided as an unsupported package in PackageHub.
Package maintainers can use the newer GCC in the internal build service, but must be aware of possible ABI issues, for example, by avoiding linking code written in different C++ standards.
Stable (libgcc, libstdc++)
Updated yearly to the versions of a new GCC major version, in all minor releases under LTS. Updates are delivered as maintenance updates.
Fully supported during General Support and LTS of each minor release.

These runtime libraries receive maintenance and security updates because they are dynamically linked by running user-space applications. They are hardened for processing untrusted input and are available for use when addressing security incidents.
Upgraded to the latest upstream version in all &suselinux; 16 minor releases under General Support or LTS.
Updated to the newest major version in all &suselinux; 16 minor releases under General Support or LTS.
Certain functionality may be removed when GDB is updated to a newer major version.
LLVM is available exclusively for use with Mesa. Any other use is not supported.
Front-ends such as Clang are not provided. They are available only from a community-supported repository.

&suse; maintains backward dynamic-linking compatibility for glibc and the C++ compiler runtime library. A binary built on an earlier &suselinux; 16 minor release runs correctly on a later minor release.
Features deprecated by upstream are removed either in newer major versions of compilers or from all toolchain components in later minor releases.
Deprecated symbols are removed from header files and are not available for link editing. Code that uses them no longer compiles or links statically.
Development tools such as the compiler are not hardened to process untrusted input.
The GCC and C++ runtime libraries are the only parts of the toolchain hardened for this purpose.
